I have no idea why this has so many positive reviews. Yes, Dead Space is an amazing game… On console. However this is the absolute worst PC Port ever released. The PC port is one of the most broken things I've ever attempted to play. KB&M controls flat-out don't work and you get insane input lag when playing with a controller. And you are stuck between two abysmal choices. You can either play at an unlocked framerate, and have shadows and lights flash in migraine inducing strobes until you reach a point in the game where your unlocked framerate breaks the games logic and you become trapped by invisible walls that you can't get around without restarting the game, and I mean restarting, as in actually starting again from the beginning. Or you can enable V-Sync and the game locks the framerate to your monitors lowest possible refresh rate, which for me was a hot 24 fps. Yes. 24 fps. Can you play a shooter at sub 30, with a controller? I sure can't. Oh, it also crashes, often. If you really need to revisit Dead Space, sadly playing on console is the only viable option. Oh, and you'll likely end up unable to refund the game because it stays running in the background after you close it. Thankfully Dead Space 2 and 3 seem to run fine.
TLDR: Great game, worst port of all time. Play it on console.

However, at the same time the side content felt less varied while falling into open world trappings of repetition and routine, most notably with the riddler. Traveller's Tales are a developer who keep iterating and refining their LEGO video game series, but seem equally insistant on focussing on the complete wrong aspects of the games. Marvel Super Heroes is in every way a better LEGO game than those that came before. The controls are better, the worlds are more fleshed out and larger, with even more side quests and replayable content than before. And if you've ever played a LEGO game before, you'll know what an accomplishment that is.
And yet, the game is an incredible mess with regards to UI and game design. Levels are confusing in what the game wants you to do. I've had to use FAQs multiple times because I found myself in an area where I had absolutely zero idea what arbitrary one time action the game wanted me to do. Traveller's Tales rely on these contextual activities more and more as the game unfolds, and while absolutely gorgous, the visual design of the levels never comes close to supporting that reliance on such arbitrary mechanics.
There are also multiple UI systems for level selecting, character swapping and gameplay mechanics that don't hold up with the sheer weight of content that has been crammed into this game.
The LEGO video games have become increasingly polished over time, and Marvel Super Heroes is undoubtably their most accomplished product to date. But they're still largely following a design structure set in place over a decade ago with the Indiana Jones series, one that was creaking at the time, and is positively falling apart these days. There's a brilliant game in here somewhere, if you add up all the great content, but the developers are asking you to do an unrealistic amount of legwork in order to enjoy yourself.

It's been a hectic ride, and the game is finally out. The development has had its ups and downs, often with the developers bringing in an update every now and then that screwed things up for many loyal fans of the original game.
As it stands now, the game is pretty much in its prime. 10 unique Perks, 1 of which is a "do anything" versatile one, plenty of maps, and a full integration with steam workshop if you wanted more.
Visually, the game never ceases to amaze. Even on mid-range pc's, it functions well, and doesn't lose too much quality as you bring the settings down. AI is smart, dodging attacks, swerving while dishing out their own to avoid even point blank shots, and a crazy variety that keeps the flow tense and varied. If you can handle it, the Flex system adds a level of gore that feels really brutal.
With almost 500 hours in, I can vouch that both solo and online modes provide hectic gameplay. On solo, which makes up most my hours, the game can be relaxing on normal and hard, tense on suicidal, and absolutedly nightmarish on hell on earth. On higher difficulties, every mistake you make the game will punish you. Every accomplishment you make will just feel like normal as you continue on. Or you can keep the difficulty limited and enjoy some blaring metal as you bring death and destruction on everything in your way. That works too.
Online, the challenge is less about surviving and more about communicating. Bigger zeds will pummel you down if you don't focus on them, while smaller zeds will swarm you if not everyone keeps the pressure off each other.
As for your bosses, you currently have volter, a gas obssessed German with an exo-suit, dual rifles, grenades, gas grenades, and a rage mode that has him spamming gas grenades while running at mach speed and rip you apart. Did I mention the gas grenades?
The Patriarch is a different story. A hulking wall of flesh from the original, his attacks are easier to dodge (probably because he warns you about what he's about to use), including a minigun, rocket launcher, invisibility, and his stomach-arm-thing.
A perfect transition for old-school fans? Probably not. A reason to transition from L4D and other horde games? Most definitely.
10/10 Would buy again.

A game that borrows a little bit of something from others, like parkour, lockpicking from Skyrim, melee, crafting, open world and does it all very-very well.
- Parkour actually requiress a bit of skill. Just going forward while pushing down a button is not enough, which is good, as it makes you feel as you actually are in control of the movement. The movement itself is dynamic: as you gain speed, you start to run and climb a bit faster. If you fall a lot - don't complain, as it's mostly your fault. Unlockable agility skills also don't hurt.
- Melee combat is heavy and you can feel the contact. You might appear underpowered at first, but with new toys you will discover a whole different flow of combat, when you can slice through multiple enemies at once, or crush them with one blow.
- Discovery is interesting, with different places and tone variation to them. The vistas are spectacular. The game also somehow manages to make you feel a bit scared of heights.
- The game, despite it's predictably boring story, has great atmosphere to it.
- The game is also quite beautiful, just be sure to tweak the options (especially the texture quality), as the default ones are often wrong for your system, and you will end up with massive stutter and freezing. One of the system I had to install it on has a fx6300 CPU and a gtx670, whith horrendous freezes and hickups once you get into the world - turns out I had to reduce the viewing distance to 0 (which still rpvides a very goo viewing distance with lots of detail), and textures to medium and it runs very well now, mostly in 38-45 range, with other setting on and medium, inculding the NVIDIA-specific ones.
- It's so rare to have a game with open world traversal and main campaign coop, not just some tack-on coop missions ( like in Far Cry 3 or4, etc...)
- There's some challenge in the game, which is a nice change from Dead Island.
As I go along, I doubt my opinion will change much, as Dying Light is almost exactly what I wanted it to be.

The beauty of the game is gradually learning from your mistakes. Getting boarded or got too many rooms on fire? Open up some hatches. Learn to priortize targets, and synchronize weapons.

The graphics really add to the atmosphere and the music is alright if nothing special, while it's enjoyable at first it simply loops for the duration of the game and becomes old rather quickly. What a long and strange trip it’s been from Arkham Asylum to Arkham City, back into the past in Arkham Origins and now for the final confrontation in Arkham Knight.
Let me say that I bought AK after the game had been pulled from stores and was extensively patched. Right now I’m running the game at maximum, including all Nvidia options for rain, etc., which should tax my graphics card to its limits. The game runs mostly fine, however. Yes, there’s some few drops below 60 fps and some micro (or macro) stuttering every time you start the game and summon a certain automobile. No idea, must be assets loading. Sucks either way. Maybe this is remedied if you install this on an SSD. In any case, the game is more than playable right now. At least for me. The game is also just stunning, graphics wise. Gotham never looked better, though it’s hard to understand why the city apparently changed its layout 3 times…
Now, first and foremost, Arkham Knight is a good game all in all. It’s most likely even the best in the series, all considering. It’s not like Arkham Origins just a rehash of the previous game, it is improved (and sometimes made worse) in almost all aspects, so here goes:
Combat:
The freeflow system has been further improved, animations are a bit smoother, the flow of combat is a bit better. However, the biggest issue I had with this game was the sometimes insane amount of enemies that get thrown at you, especially those invulnerable enemies that you have to dodge or stun or whatever. That alone wouldn’t be that bad, but the game’s camera does a VERY bad job at giving you enough overview to see exactly what’s going on. Is an enemy about to charge or fire upon you? Which enemy are you even targeting currently? And that’s another thing. One would assume that with 20 enemies present your character would attack the ones who don’t counter you, yet he likes to do that very often, which can literally mean your death when your character suddenly jumps out of view to attack a stun baton guy…Since you can only vaguely dictate which opponent to attack this is unforgivable and I can see this really having a negative effect on a higher difficulty level.
Gadgets:
These are pretty much the same, but slimmed down a bit. You now access them via a radial menu instead of the d-pad, which really interrupts the flow of the game. There’s nothing really new here…sadly.
Batmobile:
This is THE new feature in AK. You will be using the Batmobile a lot. In puzzles, in combat, in traversal…just about in every situation. You can even remote control it. The Batmobile is cool, but it a bit overused. Also at times it controls absolutely horribly…
Upgrades:
The system has been improved in comparison to AC. Of course you also get to upgrade your Batmobile! Getting every upgrade will require you to 3-star all challenges and pretty much complete the game I’d say. I’ve had about 70% of the upgrades at the end of the game I think. They’re mostly not spectacular, but pretty neat.
Enemies:
The game adds 3 new enemy types as far as hand to hand combat is concerned, if I remember correctly. There’s the drone commander, who steers a small drone that can detect you, a “big” gunner that can’t be taken out with a silent takedown, which adds a new element to predator missions, and a medic, who can revive fallen enemies.
Apart from that there’s the new drone army, which you fight in your Batmobile. Basically 4 or 5 different sorts of tanks. Those tank fights are rather boring and get annoying pretty quickly…sadly.
Collectibles:
Yes, Eddie’s back and he’s got a whopping 243 trophies, riddles, destructible objects, etc. in his arsenal. It’s going to take you ages to get them all, but at least the puzzle mechanisms are fresh and new. Too bad you still have to take out the “green” thugs to get more locations. I couldn’t bother. It’s just too much. The sad thing about this is that you not only need to collect EVERYTHING to actually fight the Riddler in this game, but to also unlock the “secret” and final ending…boooooooo. I mean it’s cool to have a reward for those soldiering through all those trophies, but something as essential as a secret ending that completely changes the ending of the game? Meh…
Challenges:
These are unlocked during the story mode, but you need to also meet a certain requirement to actually play them, for example, dive for x meters or whatever. The challenges comprise of tutorials as well as combat, predator and batmobile missions, which you can 3-star for an upgrade point. These can also be unlocked and played from the main menu once you have unlocked them. The races are the real highlights here. Those are extremely cool and fun and involve our beloved Edward.
Skins:
Once unlocked or purchased via DLC you can actually play as a different incarnation of Batman in the main game (I chose Batman of the Future I think…so edgy and works well with the Arkham Knight). There are also skins for the other playable characters as well as the Batmobile.
Main story:
This quest line is epic, you can’t deny that. It’s got everything: drama, action, slow paced segments, more drama and an incredibly good ending. I won’t spoil anything. The Arkham Knight, however, kinda got on my nerves the further the game progressed since he is by far the weakest character in the game, at least later on. He’s just boring and petulant and not really a threat, which was kinda disappointing. He also repeats himself all the time and gets more and more angry…meh.
Side quests:
There are quite a few side missions to complete, whether it’s to foil the Penguin or Two-Face, a cult preacher, a serial killer, etc. All of these missions are usually unlocked at a certain point in the game. Only the “destroy this, destroy that” missions I had to find myself more or less. The most intriguing story line is probably revolving around the Riddler, who captured poor poor Catwoman. This quest comprises of a series of riddles, challenges and races, however, Eddie will get on your nerves sooner or later. There’s only so much “herpa derpa, I’m smarter than you, you can never solve all my riddles” banter you can take…especially after having played all 4 games in a row…
Bosses:
This is probably THE weakest part of the game, because it doesn’t involve a single boss fight. Yep, that’s right. Sorry to spoiler this, but I think it’s huge. “Boss fights” in AK consist of either a) AC side mission style with an endless number of minions and the boss fighting with the group, having a health bar…b) that boss being a big♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who can only be damaged after hitting a few of the smaller minions and performing a “team takedown” or c) a tank battle. After the phenomenal boss fights of Arkham Asylum and Arkham City this is a REAL letdown…
Verdict: Good game with some improvements, but also some letdowns. Great story, good gameplay, fun elements, but a lack of diverse and interesting boss fights hurts it real bad. Get it for the conclusion of the epic storyline.
DLC: See individual story DLCs, since steam thinks this is already too long. Once again you can't change the difficulty in the DLCs...bummer. Have fun dying if you like to play on easy.

AMD GPU user review:
First off let me start by saying this game is a great deal of fun; in the first day alone I blew 7 hours into it.  However that does not come without a few issues.
Pros:
+Great Story line, a bit slower in the middle but overall wonderful.
+Movement system is quite fun, you can really tell that they put a great deal of work into it.
+Gore looks amazing and the stamina system put in place is a fair one.
+Mostly a melee game, gives you a real sense of a "post apocalyptic" metropolis.
+Map design is on spot.
Cons:
-This game is VERY demanding and it feels very poorly optimized(Running a 5820k OC'd with a raedon 295x2), 40-50fps(if lucky)
-There is currently NO support for crossfire what so ever, with this there is often in peoples games a "tearing" or "stuttering" effect, which can be eliminated if the other GPU is turned off(for the most part).
-There is really no choice based system in this game so it makes the replayability factor a little bit lower to me.
AMD users, if you DO NOT currently have a flagship/top of the line GPU wait.  I know you all want to play this game, but with its current optimization and lack of a new driver from AMD the game really isn't what it should be.  I urge you to wait for a driver update and then I will update my review and let you know.
Rollback drivers?  Did not have an effect upon gameplay at all.  14.9 was virtually the same.
Well I hope my review has helped, I'll update it in the future when new drivers come out, happy gaming!

What a long and strange trip it’s been from Arkham Asylum to Arkham City, back into the past in Arkham Origins and now for the final confrontation in Arkham Knight.
Let me say that I bought AK after the game had been pulled from stores and was extensively patched. Right now I’m running the game at maximum, including all Nvidia options for rain, etc., which should tax my graphics card to its limits. The game runs mostly fine, however. Yes, there’s some few drops below 60 fps and some micro (or macro) stuttering every time you start the game and summon a certain automobile. No idea, must be assets loading. Sucks either way. Maybe this is remedied if you install this on an SSD. In any case, the game is more than playable right now. At least for me. The game is also just stunning, graphics wise. Gotham never looked better, though it’s hard to understand why the city apparently changed its layout 3 times…
Now, first and foremost, Arkham Knight is a good game all in all. It’s most likely even the best in the series, all considering. It’s not like Arkham Origins just a rehash of the previous game, it is improved (and sometimes made worse) in almost all aspects, so here goes:
Combat:
The freeflow system has been further improved, animations are a bit smoother, the flow of combat is a bit better. However, the biggest issue I had with this game was the sometimes insane amount of enemies that get thrown at you, especially those invulnerable enemies that you have to dodge or stun or whatever. That alone wouldn’t be that bad, but the game’s camera does a VERY bad job at giving you enough overview to see exactly what’s going on. Is an enemy about to charge or fire upon you? Which enemy are you even targeting currently? And that’s another thing. One would assume that with 20 enemies present your character would attack the ones who don’t counter you, yet he likes to do that very often, which can literally mean your death when your character suddenly jumps out of view to attack a stun baton guy…Since you can only vaguely dictate which opponent to attack this is unforgivable and I can see this really having a negative effect on a higher difficulty level.
Gadgets:
These are pretty much the same, but slimmed down a bit. You now access them via a radial menu instead of the d-pad, which really interrupts the flow of the game. There’s nothing really new here…sadly.
Batmobile:
This is THE new feature in AK. You will be using the Batmobile a lot. In puzzles, in combat, in traversal…just about in every situation. You can even remote control it. The Batmobile is cool, but it a bit overused. Also at times it controls absolutely horribly…
Upgrades:
The system has been improved in comparison to AC. Of course you also get to upgrade your Batmobile! Getting every upgrade will require you to 3-star all challenges and pretty much complete the game I’d say. I’ve had about 70% of the upgrades at the end of the game I think. They’re mostly not spectacular, but pretty neat.
Enemies:
The game adds 3 new enemy types as far as hand to hand combat is concerned, if I remember correctly. There’s the drone commander, who steers a small drone that can detect you, a “big” gunner that can’t be taken out with a silent takedown, which adds a new element to predator missions, and a medic, who can revive fallen enemies.
Apart from that there’s the new drone army, which you fight in your Batmobile. Basically 4 or 5 different sorts of tanks. Those tank fights are rather boring and get annoying pretty quickly…sadly.
Collectibles:
Yes, Eddie’s back and he’s got a whopping 243 trophies, riddles, destructible objects, etc. in his arsenal. It’s going to take you ages to get them all, but at least the puzzle mechanisms are fresh and new. Too bad you still have to take out the “green” thugs to get more locations. I couldn’t bother. It’s just too much. The sad thing about this is that you not only need to collect EVERYTHING to actually fight the Riddler in this game, but to also unlock the “secret” and final ending…boooooooo. I mean it’s cool to have a reward for those soldiering through all those trophies, but something as essential as a secret ending that completely changes the ending of the game? Meh…
Challenges:
These are unlocked during the story mode, but you need to also meet a certain requirement to actually play them, for example, dive for x meters or whatever. The challenges comprise of tutorials as well as combat, predator and batmobile missions, which you can 3-star for an upgrade point. These can also be unlocked and played from the main menu once you have unlocked them. The races are the real highlights here. Those are extremely cool and fun and involve our beloved Edward.
Skins:
Once unlocked or purchased via DLC you can actually play as a different incarnation of Batman in the main game (I chose Batman of the Future I think…so edgy and works well with the Arkham Knight). There are also skins for the other playable characters as well as the Batmobile.
Main story:
This quest line is epic, you can’t deny that. It’s got everything: drama, action, slow paced segments, more drama and an incredibly good ending. I won’t spoil anything. The Arkham Knight, however, kinda got on my nerves the further the game progressed since he is by far the weakest character in the game, at least later on. He’s just boring and petulant and not really a threat, which was kinda disappointing. He also repeats himself all the time and gets more and more angry…meh.
Side quests:
There are quite a few side missions to complete, whether it’s to foil the Penguin or Two-Face, a cult preacher, a serial killer, etc. All of these missions are usually unlocked at a certain point in the game. Only the “destroy this, destroy that” missions I had to find myself more or less. The most intriguing story line is probably revolving around the Riddler, who captured poor poor Catwoman. This quest comprises of a series of riddles, challenges and races, however, Eddie will get on your nerves sooner or later. There’s only so much “herpa derpa, I’m smarter than you, you can never solve all my riddles” banter you can take…especially after having played all 4 games in a row…
Bosses:
This is probably THE weakest part of the game, because it doesn’t involve a single boss fight. Yep, that’s right. Sorry to spoiler this, but I think it’s huge. “Boss fights” in AK consist of either a) AC side mission style with an endless number of minions and the boss fighting with the group, having a health bar…b) that boss being a big♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who can only be damaged after hitting a few of the smaller minions and performing a “team takedown” or c) a tank battle. After the phenomenal boss fights of Arkham Asylum and Arkham City this is a REAL letdown…
Verdict: Good game with some improvements, but also some letdowns. Great story, good gameplay, fun elements, but a lack of diverse and interesting boss fights hurts it real bad. Get it for the conclusion of the epic storyline.
DLC: See individual story DLCs, since steam thinks this is already too long. Once again you can't change the difficulty in the DLCs...bummer. Have fun dying if you like to play on easy.

This game is amazing if you like turn based games like xcom. Have only been playing about 3 hours and love it so far. Very detailed game, with tons of options. I like the combat in xcom enemy within / unknown a bit more because you can rotate the camera and cover is always as it should be. the cover on this game is a bit weird sometimes like where a door is to the left is an obvious wall but it doesn't give you cover it you move there. Its not a big issue because it doesn't give cover, but it also does not show a cover symbom either so by not having an actual symbol you can work with that knowing exactly where to move to. It would be much nicer if the cover was always as it should appear, if a location has a wall or a bar / table you should be able to take cover from every side of the object / wall. I love how the town is very interactive, this has a huge plus over xcom. you can run around to different vendors and buildings exploring and purchasing all kinds of things. The story is very detailed as well constantly changing based on the responses that you will choose.
I picked it up because it on sale but I would definitely pay the normal price after playing this game. This and xcom enemy unknown are by far the best 2 games with this type of gameplay that I have ever ran across. I wish there was an online mode to play other players but singleplayer is still a lot of fun and so far appears like it will have huge replay value and take a while thru the campaign.
**update**
Just spent a few more hours tonight and the game keeps getting better and better the more as I play through it. The story is just so detailed and really gets you into it, very very long story with tons of twist all based on conversation choices. Some choices are only available depending on what skills you built. I had to destroy this sentry turret because my decking was not high enough to just shut it down from the box in the wall electronically. Another one you can intimidate someone which would save you money and time but only if you have 5 strength.  Another really awesome thing is that when you are not in combat its pretty much completely open and free to explore.
Earlier I compared it to xcomm, but the more I play the more it is less like xcom. The only thing like xcom is the combat which is great. Outside of combat you are free the run around, there are several items you can miss and skip if you just want to go quickly through the missions. one thing that was annoying on xcom is that even before combat you are moving in turn based on a grid, even like way before aliens are anywhere near you or actually moving. This game gets rid of the action points or "grid" type system if you arent actually in combat. Once you spot an enemy then at that point it switches to where each character gets 2 or more action points (AP) to decide what you will do in combat.  One little glitchy thing I ran across was that a spider was in a room when I opened a door and he hit 2 of my characters so I shot him back of course, but then noticed the door icon so I clicked it. The door closes and I go out of combat into normal movement and regain a nice chunk of my HP.  I don't know if it was some glitch or maybe b/c it was a spider rather than a human character it wasn't allowed to open doors therefore the game recognizes him as stuck in the room and takes me out of combat. Either way its not that big of an issue even if it does reset on a door being closed you can simply not close the doors like that in order to get a tougher experience.
The gameplay really reminds me a lot more of the old school snes / ps RPG's where you have an overhead view and all of the context is actually read. This game has no audio which kind a got to me at first, but once the story starts to get deeper its actually works very well. You spend a nice little bit of time running around to vendors or doing little side missions outside of combat which also gives it that old school RPG feel to it.  I know everyone is probably thinking thats because it actually was one. Outside of the same currency, names of classes and dialogue choices it doesn't at all feel like that game. The more I play this version the more it is starting to become one of the better games I have played. One last thing, the graphics are actually very nice and detailed. Load times for me take a while (i-3/6gb/gt640), but once you are in its a pretty large area with no other load times. If you go up an elevator there is no load time, it is only one initial load per entire mission.

Another high quality Lego take on a licensed property. Gameplay is very enjoyable, if fairly straightforward. Simple puzzles are tossed in to present a little challenge (although few would be considered tough). The storyline keeps the player moving through the levels, with Free Play offering even greater depth of play throughout. True to Lego & TT's past writing, you will find quite a few chuckles along the way.
Pros
- LOTS of characters, including Big Figs
- Lots of vehicles
- Quality voice acting (check the IMDB cast)
- Plenty of things to do, places to go, objects to SMASH
Cons (mostly minor)
- Hero flight controls - BLAH! You really should have avoided double up (dash) and double down (stop), as it makes trimming a pain
- Some pathing issues, resulting in what should be avoidable deaths. Also a couple of PC crashes while playing
- Auto, Boat, and Air vehicle spawns could have been different logos. I've seen many reports of players not getting 100%, until they remember the dock or air spawns needed to purchase remaining unlocked items
* DLC doesn't seem to have much value (unless you really want those few characters)
...also, is it just me, or do the writers not like Jean Grey (e.g. use her powers to push chairs back under a dining table?!)
